54879.subject: Chemistry
54879.text: Which among the following compounds does NOT form inter molecular hydrogen bonding?
54879.sol: Hydrogen bonding requires both a donor (H bonded to O, N, or F) and an acceptor (lone pair on O, N, or F). Ethoxy ethane ( CH₃CH₂-O-CH₂CH₃ ) contains oxygen with lone pairs, acting as an acceptor, but lacks an H-donor group. Butane ( CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ ) has no O, N, or F atoms—it cannot donate or accept hydrogen bonds. Phenol ( C₆ H₅-OH ) and butan-1-ol ( CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂ OH ) both possess -OH groups, enabling donation and acceptance of hydrogen bonds. Butane is uniquely incapable of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

6a7a1ff888e8ce35ba0d9d2c.sol: Lactose (milk sugar) is a naturally occurring disaccharide composed of -D-galactose and -D-glucose. The glycosidic linkage is formed between C₁ of the galactose unit and C₄ of the glucose unit. Because the anomeric carbon ( C₁ ) of the glucose unit is not involved in the glycosidic linkage and remains free to form a hemiacetal group in aqueous solution, lactose acts as a reducing sugar.
